A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sampler-centric oracle evaluation study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original oracle-driven sampling experiments on OpenWebText and Text8, including sampler comparisons, temperature perturbations, and conditional-generation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including the numerical comparisons in Tables 1–2 and supplementary analyses in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The Markov-chain oracle, exact HMM inference, and oracle substitutions for SEDD, MDLM, LLaDA, and ReMDM are retained. Rewritten sampler descriptions and corrected main-text formulas do not establish changes to the implemented algorithms.

E1.justification: Both evaluate token-level OpenWebText and character-level Text8. The PI, HEAD, and TAIL conditioning scenarios clarified in v2 Figure 10 already appear in v1 Appendix F.5 and Figure 9. Newly mentioned reasoning benchmarks occur only in related work.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain AR, SEDD, MDLM, LLaDA, and the same ReMDM schedule and nucleus-sampling variants. Adding MDLM to Appendix C.1's enumeration corrects a prose omission; v1 already evaluates it in Tables 1–2.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 changes the stated OWT tokenizer from standard GPT-2 byte-level BPE to a custom byte-level BPE tokenizer trained on OWT, retaining vocabulary size 4096. This revises a reported preprocessing setting; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other principal settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain SEDD temperature sensitivity, the autoregressive sharpening sanity check, ReMDM schedule/nucleus comparisons, qualitative degeneration examples, and LLaDA conditioning analyses. Expanded captions and rewritten discussion add no new ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same seed-123 entries, and qualitative examples retain their same-seed selection. No repeated-run information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 preserve their numerical entries and qualitative samples, and all nine existing plots retain identical content. Section 7.3 still reports GenPPL decreasing from 688.4 at beta = 1 to 1.27 at beta = 25. No new or corrected experimental results appear.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects SEDD's Equation 3 to explicitly compare probabilities of complete sequences and restricts ReMDM's simplified Equation 5 to unmasked tokens. These align the main text with formulas already present in v1 Appendices B and C.4. The substantive HMM, teleport, and score derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain oracle-based isolation of sampler error, persistent few-step distributional mismatch, and the unreliability of common metrics for sampler correctness. V2's conclusion additionally summarizes LLaDA coupling already argued in v1 Section 7.5, without introducing a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7.5 more cautiously attributes LLaDA behavior to interaction with the oracle's confidence structure and adds implications for denoiser training and calibration. It removes v1's explicit discussion of diversity reduction benefiting exact-answer tasks but harming coverage-dependent applications such as protein design.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 revises the tokenizer identification to a custom BPE tokenizer trained on OWT, providing materially different preprocessing information. Hardware, principal hyperparameters, and the code-access link are retained. Log-domain implementation details highlighted in v2 were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through approximate joint sampling, reasoning-oriented evaluation, and a new confidence-based-decoding discussion involving Ni et al. and Fang et al. The conclusion adds an explicit complementary relationship to Turok et al.'s DUEL. These extend the research framing beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, method explanations, results narrative, and Appendix A undergo extensive rewriting. V2 introduces a separate sampler-role subsection and finding-focused results headings. It also redundantly repeats the log-domain implementation exposition in Appendices A.7 and A.8.

P2.justification: V2 adds an overview diagram as Figure 1, relocates several existing figures and tables, and revises some captions, particularly the conditional-LLaDA caption. Existing plot graphics and table structures are retained; the visual revision is limited rather than a comprehensive redesign.

improvement.justification: The overview diagram, clearer exposition, corrected main-text sampler formulas, and more explicit tokenizer description improve understanding and technical precision. Expanded research positioning also helps contextualize the unchanged evidence. Duplicated Appendices A.7–A.8 and the shortened discussion of task-dependent diversity benefits limit the net gain.
